newsitem.title: USA: Clinton orders cut in Argentina GSP benefits.
newsitem.headline: Clinton orders cut in Argentina GSP benefits.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday ordered a reduction in the number of goods that can be imported duty free from Argentina, because he said Beunos Aires failed to adequately protect intellectual property rights.

The order, signed by Clinton during a trip to New York to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Jackie Robinson's entry into baseball, affects 50 percent of goods imported duty-free from Argentina under the Generalized System of Preferences (GSP) program. That is about $260 million worth of goods, the White House said.

"I have determined that Argentina fails to provide adequate and effective means under its laws for foreign nationals to secure, to exercise and to enforce exclusive rights in intellectual property," Clinton said in the order.
"As a result, I have determined to withdraw benefits for 50 percent (approximately $260 million) of Argentina's exports under the GSP program," he said.
The order is to go into effect 30 days after publication in the Federal Register.

Products being removed from the GSP program include chemicals, certain metals and metal products, a variety of manufactured products, and several agricultural items, including raw cane sugar, garlic, fish, milk protein concentrates and anchovies.

"The action taken today will remain in effect until Argentina takes steps to improve its (intellectual property) protection," U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said in a statement issued in Washington.
A total of 78 products that will lose duty-free treatment were listed by USTR.
She said the action was being taken because Argentina failed to bring its laws protecting patents and other intellectual property into compliance with longstanding commitments.
The United States has been pressing Argentina for years to strengthen its patent protection laws and complained that measures approved last year did not go far enough.

In January the U.S. government issued a notice that it intended to withdraw the GSP preferences. The U.S. pharmaceutical industry estimates it loses about $500 million a year to pirating of patents in Argentina.
